title: Tanzanian Pineapple Cardamom Dessert
community: Coastal Tanzania — the spiced pineapple dessert
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Tanzanian Nanasi wa Iliki — pineapple rings caramelised in a cardamom-honey pan sauce, served warm with a dusting of cinnamon. Tanzania's most effortless hot fruit dessert — the pineapple's natural acidity caramelises magnificently in a hot pan.
longDesc: Caramelised pineapple with cardamom is the fastest hot dessert in Tanzania — pineapple rings in a hot pan with honey and cardamom for 5 minutes produces a dessert of genuine quality. The pineapple's bromelain breaks down as it cooks, its natural sugars caramelise, and the cardamom perfumes everything.
ingredients: 1 ripe pineapple — peeled, cored, sliced into rings
// Serve with: coconut ice cream (TZA164) or yogurt
steps: Heat coconut oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Add pineapple rings in a single layer.
Cook without moving for 3—4 minutes until golden caramelised.
Add honey, cardamom, cinnamon, and salt. Toss to coat.
Cook 1 more minute until honey bubbles and glazes.
Add lime juice. Remove from heat.
Serve immediately with coconut ice cream.
chefTips: Do not move the pineapple — contact time creates caramelisation.
Lime at the end brightens everything.
commonMistakes: Low heat — steams instead of caramelises.
cookingScience: Pineapple contains 12—15% natural sugars. When pan-cooked at high temperature, these sugars caramelise (above 160°C) through pyrolysis reactions — producing hundreds of flavour compounds including diacetyl and furans. The bromelain enzyme denatures above 60°C, which is why cooked pineapple is sweeter and less acidic than raw.
sustainabilityTips: Tanzania produces excellent pineapple in the coastal and highland regions.
healthBenefits: Very low calorie without ice cream.
culturalNote: Caramelised pineapple is Tanzania's quick-assembly dessert — the fruit that grows abundantly, cooked in 10 minutes into something that can be served at the finest table. It represents the confidence of Tanzania's modern food culture.
